{"segments":[{"text":"Schooling in Luxembourg follows three distinct tracks, and the choice should be prepared well before the move itself.","kind":"transition"},{"text":"This is described as the longest and most constrained step of the whole settling-in process, and one that should be started before even looking for housing.","kind":"factuel","claim_ids":["c1"]},{"text":"The public school system is free and teaches in Luxembourgish first, then introduces German and French; it integrates young arrivals very well, though a later arrival can face a real language barrier that needs honest evaluation.","kind":"factuel","claim_ids":["c2"]},{"text":"Alongside public schools, European schools follow a curriculum leading to the European Baccalaureate (priority for children of EU institution staff, others admitted subject to availability and a tuition fee), free public international schools with English, French or German sections that are highly sought after, and private schools offering the International Baccalaureate or foreign curricula at significant cost.","kind":"factuel","claim_ids":["c3"]},{"text":"Registering with the commune generally comes before school registration, spots in the most sought-after sections can fill up a year in advance, and it is important to check availability of the specific language section rather than just the school itself; before leaving your home country, you should also obtain a certificate of deregistration and recent report cards from the previous school.","kind":"factuel","claim_ids":["c4"]},{"text":"The documents provided do not specify exact application deadlines or contact details for each individual school or section, so those steps would need to be confirmed directly with the chosen institution.","kind":"limite"}],"claims":[{"claim_id":"c1","text":"School registration is the longest and most constrained step of the settling-in process and should be started before the housing search.","quotes":[{"block_id":"lux-guide:fecole:3","quote":"C'est la démarche la plus longue et la plus contrainte de toute l'installation, et celle qu'il faut engager en premier, avant même la recherche de logement."}]},{"claim_id":"c2","text":"Public school alphabetizes in Luxembourgish then introduces German and French, integrates young children well, but poses a real language barrier for later arrivals.","quotes":[{"block_id":"lux-guide:fecole:5","quote":"L'enseignement public luxembourgeois alphabétise en luxembourgeois, puis introduit l'allemand, puis le français. Il intègre remarquablement bien les enfants arrivés jeunes."}]},{"claim_id":"c3","text":"European, international public, and private schools each offer different curricula, admission priorities, and costs.","quotes":[{"block_id":"lux-guide:fecole:7","quote":"Les écoles européennes proposent un cursus par section linguistique menant au baccalauréat européen. L'accès est prioritaire pour les enfants de personnels des institutions européennes ; les autres familles sont admises selon les places disponibles et acquittent un minerval."}]},{"claim_id":"c4","text":"Commune registration usually precedes school registration, sections can fill a year ahead, and you must check section availability and collect a deregistration certificate and report cards before leaving.","quotes":[{"block_id":"lux-guide:fecole:9","quote":"L'inscription à la commune précède généralement l'inscription scolaire, et les places dans les sections les plus recherchées partent parfois un an à l'avance."}]}]}
